findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record why monotonic sequential ADR numbering is retained (e.g. human-citability, backward-compat with existing 'ADR NNNN' prose references) rather than switching to collision-free identifiers (ULID/UUID or date-prefixed slugs), so the marker-file mechanism and the 22-file renumbering are justified against the root-cause alternative.
evidence: The plan enumerates and rejects only two alternatives — a pre-merge CI counter check ('racy by construction') and a shared sorted index ('conflicts on EVERY concurrent addition') — but never the option of dropping monotonic numbers.

Collision-free identifiers are a well-trodden approach for distributed/concurrent id allocation; a retrieved source (Zalando RESTful API Guidelines, opensource.zalando.com/restful-api-guidelines) explicitly favours ULID for time-ordered ids, and date-prefixed ADR filenames are a common ADR-tooling convention.

The chosen design incurs a one-time 22-file renumbering migration plus a permanent marker-file bijection that a root-cause id-scheme change would avoid entirely — a cost the plan never compares against.
findings.finding: The plan fixes monotonic sequential ADR numbering as an unquestioned premise and never considers the most established alternative to sequence-number collisions: collision-free identifiers (ULID/UUID, or timestamp/date-prefixed slugs) that eliminate the collision class at its root instead of preserving numbering and layering a conflict-forcing marker file plus a 22-file renumbering migration on top of it.
findings.location: Design section 'Prevention is git's, not CI's' and 'Renumbering is approved'
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer asks why the repo keeps racy sequential numbers plus a compensating conflict mechanism rather than adopting non-colliding ids and retiring the whole collision problem.
New ADRs continue to require a .numbers/NNNN marker and CI bijection assertion in perpetuity, a maintenance surface a non-sequential scheme would not carry.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Alternatives' subsection noting that non-sequential ids (ULID/date-prefixed) were considered and rejected because existing bare 'ADR NNNN' references (AGENTS.md:42, CONTRIBUTING.md commit trailers) and human citability require short stable sequential numbers, so the collision class is contained via the .numbers/ marker rather than eliminated by re-identifying every ADR.

No AC calls for an ADR documenting the .numbers/ mechanism; the ACs only require the markers, the CI check, README.md, and RENUMBERING.md
findings.finding: The plan introduces a NEW architectural mechanism — the per-number marker file docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN whose add/add conflict enforces uniqueness — but no acceptance criterion or step records this decision in an ADR itself, despite this being an ADR-management repo where such decisions are conventionally captured (and ADR 0047's rebase behavior is a direct input).
scenarios: A future contributor sees .numbers/ files, doesn't understand the add/add-conflict rationale, and 'cleans them up' or regenerates them
The rejection of the shared-index approach is lost and someone re-proposes it
findings.suggested_fix: Author a new ADR at the top of the 0070-0091 band documenting the marker-file decision, referencing ADR 0047, and record its marker like any other ADR.
